newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Trial of Ethiopia's former military junta resumes.
newsitem.headline: Trial of Ethiopia's former military junta resumes.

text.p: Prosecution witnesses told a court on Tuesday that Ethiopia's former military junta jailed and killed their relatives without any trial.
They testified as a trial resumed, after a two-month break, for 71 members of the Dergue, the junta that overthrew Emperor Haile Selassie in 1974 and ruled until 1991.
A total of 46 former officials of the Dergue were in the dock on Tuesday. Twenty-five others, including former Marxist ruler Mengistu Haile Mariam, are on trial in absentia.

Colonel Kifle Belay, 55, a former police officer, said his brother Mamo Belay was jailed at the central crime investigation office in the Ethiopian capital in 1975 on suspicion of being a member of the then-banned Ethiopian Peoples Revolutionary Party.

He said his family was allowed to deliver food for Mamo, a student, before suddenly being told he was not there. Kifle said his brother never had a trial and his family did not know how and when was killed.
"We were not given his body. We were only told by prison officials that he was dead," Kifle told the Addis Ababa court.
Housewife Asegedetch Gebre Wahid testified that her nephew Tadewos Zegeye, who lived with her, disappeared in January 1975 after leaving home to attend a rally.

After a long search, she dicovered Tadewos was held at the central crime investigation office and started taking food and clothes to him. After about four months, warders told her not to bring any more because he was not there.
She said her family presumed he was dead because he had not been heard of since.
The third prosecution witness on Tuesday, Abeba Araya, said her husband Hailu Addis was jailed at the same office and she did not know why.
She said her father-in-law visited her husband in jail as she was in hospital giving birth. She said her father-in-law was finaly told Hailu had gone and some of his clothes were returned.
Abeba said her family had not received Hailu's body and as far as they were concerned he had not been tried in a court.

The government says it is holding 1,700 prisoners for alleged crimes under the Dergue. The only ones charged are those now on trial, and the 46 present have all pleaded not guilty. The rest have been held for up to five years without charge.
The trial was adjourned until next Tuesday.
